title: Grove needs an explicit Atlas authorization even to collect fees accrued on its own Uniswap position
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.2.3.1 records, under *Instance-specific Operational Processes*, that "Grove is authorized to execute a **one-time** collect of all fees accrued on this Instance's Uniswap V3 position (tokenId 1192575 in the Uniswap V3 `NonfungiblePositionManager`), with proceeds received by the **ALM Proxy**."

Every element of that sentence narrows it: one-time rather than standing, a named tokenId rather than the Instance's positions generally, and a fixed destination for the proceeds. Collecting fees the position has already earned is about as economically benign as an action gets — it does not change exposure, take counterparty risk, or move price — and yet it required a written grant scoped to a single NFT.

The generalizable claim is about the shape of Grove's mandate. An Agent operating under *residual* discretion would need no such entry: anything not forbidden would be permitted, and fee collection would obviously not be forbidden. That this authorization had to be added establishes the opposite default — Grove's powers are **enumerated**, and an action outside the rate-limited conduits defined by the standard schema is unauthorized until the Atlas says otherwise.

The trade-off is direct: enumeration makes the Agent's authority auditable and its overreach detectable, at the cost of routing routine housekeeping through governance. The "one-time" qualifier shows the cost being paid rather than avoided — the cheaper move would have been a standing authorization, and it was not taken.
description: A one-time collect on a specific Uniswap V3 tokenId, with proceeds routed to the ALM Proxy, is written into the Instance document — evidence Grove holds enumerated powers, not residual discretion.
